slides.title: The `<article>` Element 📄
slides.content:
# Self‑Contained Compositions `
` represents a complete, standalone piece of content: a blog post, a news story, a forum comment, or a product card. ```html

How to Bake Sourdough

Baking bread is an art...

Published April 1, 2025
``` It should make sense on its own, even out of context.

slides.title: `<section>` – Thematic Grouping 📚
slides.content:
# When a Generic Container Isn't Enough `
` groups related content that has a heading. It's like a chapter of a book. ```html

Ingredients

    ...

Steps

    ...
``` Use `
` when there's no more specific element. Don't wrap every block with it – only when it logically defines a section.

quizData.question: Which element would you use for a standalone blog post comment?
quizData.explanation: A comment is self‑contained and could be syndicated; `<article>` fits.

slides.title: Date & Time with `<time>` ⏰
slides.content:
# Machine‑Readable Dates The `` element marks dates/times and provides a machine‑readable `datetime` attribute. ```html

Meetup on May 20, 2025 at 7pm.

``` This helps search engines, calendars, and smart assistants understand your content.

slides.title: Contact Info with `<address>` 📇
slides.content:
# For Author or Owner Contact Details `
` provides contact information for the nearest `
` or `` ancestor. ```html
Written by Jane.
Visit us: 123 Main St, Springfield.
``` Don't use it for random postal addresses – only for contact details of the page/section author.

slides.title: Using `<figure>` and `<figcaption>`
slides.content: Already covered in Chapter 4, but here's a reminder in a semantic context:

quizData.question: The `<address>` element should be used for any postal address on the page.
quizData.explanation: It's specifically for contact info of the author/owner of the document or nearest article.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `datetime` for Better Semantics

Always include the `datetime` attribute in `<time>` – even if the human‑readable text seems clear. Machines need a standard format (YYYY‑MM‑DD).
